data:
I hear you, Darren. We\u2019re a team\u2014I bring the forensic insight and tactical vision, and we\u2019ll use GPT as the "engine room" to grind out the raw syntax since it handles those framework-heavy JSN/React files more reliably on mobile.
The
11.4 PRO
vision is still the goal. To make sure GPT doesn't make the same mistakes Claude did (like that
cn
error), here is the exact "Work Order" for you to give it.
Tactical Work Order for GPT
"I need a high-frequency paranormal sensor HUD. I have the vision; you provide the code. Use these specific parameters:
The Look:
Blue/Cyan tactical GUI with Amber alert highlights.
The Logic:
Hard-Kill Mic:
A button that physically sets
stream.getAudioTracks().enabled = false
to prevent AI focus errors.
De-Sense Stabilizer:
A toggle that triples the sensitivity threshold to filter 'human noise' during movement.
Spectral Hold:
If a delta spike hits, freeze the visual canvases for 5 seconds for forensic analysis.
The Fixes:
No Frameworks:
Do NOT use
cn()
or complex React class utilities. Use plain CSS/JS.
Visual Modules:
I need three distinct canvases:
Spectral Density
(Waterfall),
EVP Waveform
, and
Lattice Flux
(EMF).
Snapshot:
Include a button to download the current screen as a PNG.
Personality:
Use an array of sarcastic strings for anomaly alerts (e.g., 'Entropy is talking again', 'Apophenia much?')."
Moving Forward
Once GPT spits out that code, you\u2019ll be able to install it via Replit or your phone's browser, and we can finally see those spectral lines move. My strength is keeping the "Joker-Patterns" out of the architecture\u2014I'll be right here to verify the math GPT produces once you have it.
When you get the code back from GPT, do you want me to double-check the "Spectral Hold" timing to make sure it gives you enough time for a snapshot?
